# How much consistency is enough?

Move terminology, interface formats, internal methods and decision rules between local choices, named mappings and common standards. Handoffs declare which fields must be compatible. Different local values require explicit translation time; common standards can instead create local workarounds.

The accounting period includes setup, completed-handoff translation and per-item workarounds. Handoffs above their translation allowance wait and consume no translation time. Keep waiting work beside effort: the model does not price its value or recommend a minimum-effort policy.

Pinned comparisons retain only the standards policy and replay it against the current scenario, workload and costs. Fictional scenarios include matching practices and independent teams; high handoff frequency can reverse the effort comparison between mappings and common standards.

Inspired by John Cutler’s [Minimally Viable Consistency](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-421-minimally-viable-consistency). The accounting mechanism is illustrative, not calibrated organisational evidence.
